messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: gpu-pool-availability degraded in us-west-2. Severity: P1. Symptom: sustained queue growth + request throttles. Auto-escalation to #incidents at 1748888888. Page on-call.
jordan: I'm on it. seeing spike in gpu-queue length across pool 'redwood-gpu-prod-1' — queue ~1.4k increasing. latency p95 from 320ms -> 1.2s. error rate on generation endpoints jumping to 11% (503/429 surface). starting triage.
ria: ack. do we have autoscaler logs? last known desired replicas is 8 but actual stuck at 8, scale_up attempts failing with rate limit from cloud provider earlier.
kevin: grabbing autoscaler controller logs. tailing now.
kevin: paste: ```2026-03-15T02:34:21Z controller autoscaler: scale_up request for pool redwood-gpu-prod-1 replicas=12 reason=queue_growth error=response: 429 QuotaExceeded provider: gpunodes quota``` 
kevin: looks like provider-side quota limits hit. also seeing intermittent provider API 502s for scale requests.
leila: customer impact: internal monitoring shows ~4% of requests got 503s in last 6m and some mid-tier customers reporting timeouts. adding customer-impact tag.
ops-bot: Notifying support: support-ticket 2468 created for customer-facing comms. Template: "We are experiencing degraded generation throughput..." (sent to Support).
jordan: mitigation options: 1) evict best-effort / lower-priority tenants from the pool, 2) bump routing to failover region (eu-west-1) for new requests, 3) enable burst capacity via reserved fallback nodes (if available), 4) temporarily enable model-variant CPU fallback for non-latency critical requests.
ria: can we evict safely? what's the low-priority tenant list for this pool?
kevin: querying scheduler. low-priority tenants identified: internal-ci, batch-embeddings-nonprod, long-running-async. eviction would free ~3 nodes worth of capacity.
leila: recommend evict internal-ci and batch-embeddings-nonprod first. communicate to tenant owners. set eviction TTL 5m.
jordan: doing eviction now. ```/bin/redwoodctl evict --pool redwood-gpu-prod-1 --tenants internal-ci,batch-embeddings-nonprod --grace 300s``` 
ops-bot: Eviction job queued. Watch logs: job-evict-7592.
kevin: autoscaler still failing to create new nodes due to quota. evictions should reduce queue but won't solve long-term if demand keeps rising.
ria: enable eu failover for read-only/embeddings routes now? implications for latency.
jordan: routing rule applied: route generation requests from new sessions -> fallback-region eu-west-1 for low-latency-tolerant customers. ```/config/routing apply --match "tier:standard AND region:us-west-2" --fallback eu-west-1``` 
leila: sent customer comms draft to support; we'll mention mitigation steps and ETA ~30-45m.
oncall-bot: Incident channel bridgecall suggested. React with :phone: to join. (2 reactions)
devex-mgr: joining bridgecall. I'll take notes for postmortem and SLO checks.
kevin: metrics update: after eviction queue dropped from 1.4k -> 820 in 2m. p95 latency down to 760ms. errors trending down but still higher than normal.
ria: good. still seeing a backlog for some pinned sessions (dedicated customers) — need targeted eviction or migration.
jordan: checking pinned session list. pinned sessions for tenant 'acme-corp' on pool redwood-gpu-prod-1 are 6 sessions; acme has SLA. we can't evict them. planning to route new acme sessions to fallback reserved capacity in eu-west-1? need ops approval.
leila: ops approves temporary cross-region for new sessions only. existing pinned sessions remain. notify account team.
kevin: cloud provider updated quota case, but ETA unknown. raising alternative: spin up preemptible nodes in another AZ to relieve immediate pressure.
ria: what's impact of preemptible on inference reliability? we can use them for background jobs and non-critical requests.
jordan: enabling preemptible pool connect as overflow for low-priority traffic. ```/infra/scale --pool preemptible-overflow --nodes 6 --reason "incident overflow"``` 
ops-bot: Preemptible pool requested. Cloud scheduling Id: req-7890. Preemptible nodes registering...
kevin: nodes are registering. adding to routing pool for non-SLA traffic only. queue further down to 290. p95 now 280ms for routed traffic, overall p95 600ms.
leila: support updated customers: "we have routed non-critical traffic to overflow pools and are working with cloud provider on quota" — posted to support ticket.
devex-mgr: note: we saw multiple autoscaler errors at 02:33 and 02:35 with provider 429/502. need to capture these in postmortem and timeline.
ria: jordan, can you start an incident timeline doc? include root cause hypothesis: provider quota + autoscaler retries not gracefully degrading to alternative pools.
jordan: creating timeline (linked in incident doc). adding entries for eviction, routing change, preemptible bring-up, provider quota case creation.
kevin: still seeing occasional 429 from provider on scale calls — backoff logic in autoscaler seems conservative; it retries but gives up at 5 attempts. we failed to implement fast-failover to overflow pool when scale_up control plane errors occur.
ria: that's critical. action item: autoscaler should trigger fallback policy after N consecutive provider failures (N=2).
leila: customer metrics: top affected customers (by error volume): acme-corp (partial), beta-startup (timeouts), internal-api-monitoring (drops). most severe window 02:32–02:45 UTC.
ops-bot: Status page updated: "Partial degradation in us-west-2; some generation requests may see increased latency or errors. Mitigations in progress." (posted)
jordan: proposing post-incident actions now:
- ACTION 1: Autoscaler fallback: implement policy to route to overflow pools after 2 provider scale_up failures. Owner: kevin. Due: 2 weeks.
- ACTION 2: Alerting thresholds: add alert for sustained queue growth >600 for 5m with autoscaler inability to scale. Owner: ria. Due: 3 days.
- ACTION 3: Provisioning safety: request higher provider quota and add runbook for rapid quota cases. Owner: leila. Due: 1 week.
- ACTION 4: Per-tenant eviction policies: add safe-eviction list and notify flows to avoid evicting SLA tenants. Owner: jordan. Due: 1 week.
- ACTION 5: Chaos test: add synthetic quota-failure test to CI to ensure fallback triggers. Owner: devex-mgr. Due: 3 weeks.
kevin: will include logs and a minimal repro for autoscaler in action item notes.
ria: wrapping up — queue stable at ~120, errors 0.8% last 5m. Support will follow up to customers. I'll take the incident handoff to the next oncall.
jordan: handing off to ria for post-incident follow-up. thanks everyone.
ria: taking it. final note: we should schedule a postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC. invite: eng-runtime, eng-sre, product-ops, support.
oncall-bot: Incident resolved -> status: mitigated. Closing bridgecall. Duration ~18m."
